observations:
Torah #260 is a very short, tightly unified teaching with a single conceptual cluster. The entire argument revolves around one bechina equation: שֵׁם = נֶפֶשׁ = מְפֻרְסָם. There are no independent conceptual domains in the source text that could form a second package.

The other concepts mentioned in the Torah — יִחוּד (divine union), עֲשָׂרָה הֲרוּגֵי מַלְכוּת (the Ten Martyrs), שְׁכִינָה (the Shechina), יִשְׂרָאֵל (Israel), and הֲרִיגָה (killing) — all appear in eitza (causal/contextual) roles: souls ascending through self-sacrifice produces (eitza) the divine union; the Tzaddik's sacrifice of his שֵׁם saves (eitza) Israel. These are narrative flow elements that connect TO the central package, not independent bechina clusters.

Specifically:
- יִחוּד is the goal/result of מְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ — a classic eitza relationship.
- שְׁכִינָה is the destination to which the souls return — again eitza.
- יִשְׂרָאֵל and שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים (bloodshed) describe the social and physical consequences — eitza.

For a new package to be warranted, there would need to be 3 or more concepts connected by explicit 'X הוא בְּחִינַת Y' language that form a domain distinct from שֵׁם/נֶפֶשׁ/מְפֻרְסָם. No such cluster exists in this Torah. The teaching is complete with one package.
